answer: Seed-honeypot panels blunt the one-mind-many-masks sybil: each epoch plants decoy challenges—say, pricing a copper token or naming a meadow herb like yarrow—whose wording is trap-randomized per identity. Masks driven by one shared inference pipeline emit suspiciously correlated reasoning traces on these decoys, so a correlation detector collapses them into a single author. To dodge it, an attacker must run a genuinely distinct model-and-prompt stack per mask, turning one cheap fan-out into many independent compute bills.
